CITY OF INGLEWOOD
  ECONOMIC AND COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT DEPARTMENT
  PLANNING COMMISSION
  MEETING AGENDA
September 1, 2021 7:00 P.M.
City Council Chambers – Ninth Floor (Planning Commission & Staff)
1 West Manchester Boulevard

  COVID-19 PUBLIC PARTICIPATION OPTIONS

Due to the existing COVID-19 health emergency and the social
distancing measures currently in effect, and pursuant to the
Governor’s Executive Order N-29-20 (https://www.gov.ca.gov/wp-
content/uploads/2020/03/3.17.20-N-29-20-EO.pdf), please note that
members of the public will only be allowed to observe and address
the Planning Commission Meeting of September 1, 2021 at 7:00 P.M.
by video and other electronic means, as follows:

In Person:  The Library Lecture Hall (located adjacent to the Main
Library at 101 Manchester Boulevard) will be open to provide members of
the public with an opportunity to address the Planning Commission on
Agenda Items.

Viewing and Listening to the Meeting without Making Public Comments: On
Spectrum Cable Local Channel 35 with audio and limited video. Please
check with your cable provider for details.

Written Public Comments: Members of the public can submit comments for
consideration by the Planning Commission by sending them to Mindy Wilcox,
AICP, Planning Manager at mwilcox@cityofinglewood.org. To ensure
distribution to the members of the Planning Commission prior to
consideration of the agenda, comments must be received prior to 12:00
P.M. on September 1, 2021, the day of the meeting. Correspondence should
indicate the meeting date and agenda item. Comments received after 12:00
P.M. and prior to close of the public hearing will be made part of the
official public record of the meeting.

Accessibility: If you will require special accommodations due to a
disability, please contact the Planning Division Office at (310) 412-
5230, One Manchester Boulevard, 4th Floor, Inglewood, California 90301.
All requests for accommodations must be received 48 hours prior to the
day of the hearing.

[Agenda Items and Additional Public Access Options Listed on
Following Pages]
 1.  Pledge of Allegiance.

2.  Roll Call.

3.  Communications from staff.

4.  Public Comments Regarding Agenda Items. Persons wishing to
  address the Planning Commission on any item on the agenda
  other than a public hearing may do so at this time.

5.  PUBLIC HEARINGS
  A continued public hearing to consider an application by J.
  D. Fox, representing WDR, LLC, for AT&T, for Special Use
  Permit No. 2021-007 (SP-2021-007) to allow the location of a
  roof-mounted wireless telecommunication facility on the roof
  of an existing parking garage on an approximately 3.6-acre,
  HPSP(Hollywood Park Specific Plan) zoned property at 3863
  West Century Boulevard.
  Preliminary Recommendations:
  1) Affirm the categorical exemption EA-CE-2021-055; and
  2) Adopt the attached resolution approving SP-2021-007,
  subject to 15 conditions, and/or add conditions as
  deemed appropriate.

6.  Public Comments. Anyone wishing to address the Planning
  Commission on any matter within their jurisdiction and not
  elsewhere considered on the agenda may do so at this time.

7.  Commission Initiatives.

8.  Adjournment.

In the event that the Planning Commission meeting of September 1,
2021 is not held, or is concluded prior to a public hearing or
other agenda item being considered, the public hearing or non-
public hearing agenda item will automatically be continued to the
next regular Planning Commission meeting.

Hearing  materials  are  available  at
https://www.cityofinglewood.org/AgendaCenter/Planning-
Commission-4 and at City Hall, 1st Floor Lobby Information Desk
during regular business hours. If any additional documents are
received for distribution to the Planning Commission after
publication of this Agenda but before 12:00 P.M. on the day of the
meeting, they will be made available for public inspection at the
following  webpage
https://www.cityofinglewood.org/AgendaCenter/Planning-
Commission-4.

(Note: The above procedures are subject to change for future
Commission meetings. Please refer to future Planning Commission
agendas for public participation option procedures at that time.)

 Special Use Permit No. 2021-007 (SP-2021-007)  September 1, 2021
3863 West Century Boulevard

REQUEST
The applicant, J.D. Fox, representing WDR, LLC. for AT&T Mobility, is requesting
approval to allow the location of a roof-mounted wireless telecommunications facility on
the roof of an existing parking garage.

BACKGROUND
The Inglewood Municipal Code (IMC), Chapter 12, Articles 10.1, 25, and 31, requires
approval of a Special Use Permit (SUP) for the installation of a wireless
telecommunication facility in specified zones in the City, when in compliance with Article
31 of Chapter 12 of the IMC.

On July 21, 2021, the Planning Commission meeting was cancelled due to technical
difficulties that prevented members of the public from listening to and participating in the
meeting. The item was automatically continued to August 4, 2021.

On August 4, 2021, the Planning Commission voted to continue the item to September
1, 2021, to allow the applicant additional time to answer technology specific questions.

On August 26, 2021, the applicant submitted a letter to provide additional information
regarding the project. This letter is included as Attachment 4.

DISCUSSION
Site Characteristics and Existing Use
The approximately 3.96 acre site is located on the north side of Century Boulevard and
is located within the Hollywood Park Specific Plan. The properties to the north, east,
and west of the subject site are also zoned HPSP and properties to south, across
Century Boulevard, are zoned M-1L (Limited Manufacturing) and located in the Sports
and Entertainment Overlay Zone.

The subject structure is an approximately 450,000 square-foot, three story parking
structure that provides four levels of parking with approximately 1,410 parking spaces
for the adjacent Hollywood Park Casino. The parking structure’s existing roofline is 48-
feet at its highest point and the building has a midcentury modern architectural style.
The casino development includes the casino building, parking garage, surface parking,
and landscaping.

The applicant proposes to install four spherical antennas, 12 panel antennas, 58
Remote Radio Units (RRUs), and associated equipment installed behind new screening
on the building rooftop. Four radio cabinets and utilities will also be installed at grade
level located in the rear of the building. The proposed rooftop screening is designed to
match the existing parking structure design and will shield the equipment from being
seen from any public right of way. The location was selected by the applicant because
AT&T’s radio-frequency engineers are preparing for the large volume of activity at SoFi
 Special Use Permit No. 2021-007 (SP-2021-007)  September 1, 2021
3863 West Century Boulevard
Page 3 of 5

Stadium, Hollywood Park, and the upcoming LA Clippers’ arena. According to the
applicant, they have identified a lack of cellular capacity in the area which will cause
congestion on the network. The new site will reduce the load on existing surrounding
cell sites.

Architectural Screening
The IMC requires that screening for roof-mounted wireless telecommunications facilities
and accessory equipment be designed to be consistent with the surrounding buildings,
structures, and/or landscaping. On the subject site, all roof mounted equipment is
proposed to be screened behind proposed architectural features.

The applicant proposes to screen the roof mounted equipment with screen walls that
have a maximum height of eleven-feet, three-inches above the top of the existing
structure. The proposed screen walls will be painted in a color and texture to match the
existing building design, architectural style, color palette, and existing rooftop
projections. These walls will screen the antennae and equipment associated with the
proposed telecommunications facility from the commercial corridor along Century
Boulevard and from the surrounding developments. The screen walls will appear to be
part of the original parking structure design.

The proposed 447 square-foot ground equipment enclosure is located next to the
parking structure on the north/rear side of the building. This area will house all needed
ground equipment such as radio cabinets and utilities. If approved, the applicant will be
required to modify the enclosure screening during Plot Plan Review to ensure that all
Hollywood Park Specific Plan and IMC development requirements are met.

Parking and Landscaping
The existing landscaping and parking garage are well maintained. Any required
modifications to landscaping and parking will be considered as part of the Plot Plan
Review process. The casino requires 1,467 parking spaces. The existing parking
garage provides 1,410 spaces and surface parking lot provides 167 spaces, totaling
1,577 parking spaces; therefore, there is a surplus of 110 parking spaces. The
proposed telecommunications facility will occupy 12 parking spaces on the top level of
the parking garage and the applicant will be assigned the use of one (1) surface parking
space for the maintenance of the equipment, allowing for a continued surplus of 97
parking spaces.

Proposed Wireless Providers
AT&T is a public utility company that is licensed and regulated by the California Public
Utilities Commission (CPUC) as an authorized telecommunications service provider for
California. They operate 15 wireless telecommunications sites, including small cell and
indoor sites, in Inglewood, four (4) of which are located within one (1) mile of the subject
site. The applicant has indicated that the proposed telecommunications facility will
improve the service capabilities within the AT&T system and in the Inglewood area.
 Special Use Permit No. 2021-007 (SP-2021-007)  September 1, 2021
3863 West Century Boulevard
Page 4 of 5

There are seven (7) wireless telecommunications facilities operated by other providers
within one-mile of the subject site, as shown in the table below.

  Table 1: Wireless Telecommunications Facilities Within One Mile of Subject Site
  Operator  Address  Facility Type  Approval
 SBA  3141 Century Boulevard  Tree  SP-892
 LA SMSA  10922 S Prairie Avenue  Monopole  SP-1212
 STC One  3742 W. Century Boulevard  Monopole  SP-876
 LA SMSA  3738 West Century Boulevard  Monopole  SP-1024
 CCTM  3730 W. Century Boulevard  Monopole  SP-765
 SBA  923 S. Prairie Avenue  Monopole  SP-1077
 T-Mobile  9817-1/2 Crenshaw Boulevard  Utility Pole  Public Right of Way
  Source: City of Inglewood Planning Division Records (06/2021)

Section 704 of Title 7, of The Federal Communications Act of 1996, states that no state
or local government may regulate the placement, construction, and modification of
personal wireless service facilities on the basis of the environmental effects of radio
frequency emissions to the extent that such facilities comply with FCC regulations.

Area Compatibility
The segment of Century Boulevard where the subject site is located is developed with
commercial and industrial uses. The addition of an architecturally screened wireless
telecommunications facility is not anticipated to alter the character or use of the corridor
and will be compatible with surrounding uses. The associated architectural screening
would be consistent with the architectural style of the existing parking structure.

Plot Plan Review Required
If the Planning Commission approves the request, the applicant will be required to
complete the Plot Plan Review process. The proposed plans are required to comply
with all applicable provisions of the Zoning Code and receive approval from the
Planning Division, the Public Works Department, the Los Angeles County Fire
Department, and any other applicable City departments. Additionally, the plans must
comply with applicable regulations of the Federal Communications Committee (FCC),
the California Public Utilities Commission (CPUC), the operational standards of
American National Standards Institute (ANSI) and the Institute of Electrical Engineers
(IEE).

Public Comments
As of the preparation of this report, no public comments in favor or against this project
have been received.

MINUTES
  INGLEWOOD PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
  WEDNESDAY, SEPTEMBER 1, 2021

(1) PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE:

The City of Inglewood Planning Commission held its Planning
Commission meeting on Wednesday, September 1, 2021, in the Council
Chambers, on the ninth floor, in City Hall. Following the Pledge
of Allegiance by Commissioner Cheryl Shaw-Williams, the meeting
was called to order at 7:00 p.m.

(2) ROLL CALL:

Present:  Chairman Larry Springs
  Commissioner Patricia Patrick
  Commissioner David Rice
  Commissioner Aide Trejo
  Commissioner Cheryl Shaw-Williams

Staff:  Christopher E. Jackson, Sr., E&CD Director
  Mindy Wilcox, AICP, Planning Manager
  Bernard McCrumby, Senior Planner
  Jeff Lewis, Assistant City Attorney
  Marissa Fewell, Planner
  Angel Leon-Martell, Assistant Planner
  Sean May, Planning Technician
  Evangeline Lane, Secretary
  Via Community Phone Call Coverage:
  AT&T Conference Call Operator Rep.

(3) STAFF COMMUNICATIONS:

Ms. Wilcox stated - No communications from staff.

(4) PUBLIC COMMENTS:

None (Confirmed by AT&T Operator)

(5) PUBLIC HEARINGS:

5A: SPECIAL USE PERMIT NO. 2021 (SP-2021-007), 3863 WEST CENTURY
BOULEVARD.
A continued public hearing to consider an application by J. D.
Fox, representing WDR, LLC, for AT&T, for Special Use Permit No.
2021-007 (SP-2021-007) to allow the location of a roof-mounted
wireless telecommunication facility on the roof of an existing
parking garage on an approximately 3.6-acre, HPSP(Hollywood Park
Specific Plan) zoned property at 3863 West Century Boulevard.

Ms. Marissa Fewell, Planner, made the staff presentation.

Chairman Springs asked the applicant to come forward to address
the Planning Commission and speak about his project.

Mr. J. D. Fox addressed the planning commission about how they
plan on operating the Antennas and how they will provide cellular
service to the So-Fi Stadium parking lot, the Hollywood Park
Casino, traffic along Century Boulevard as well as the added
benefit to the surrounding community.

Chairman Springs asked the Planning Commission if they had any
questions for the applicant.
 Inglewood Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
September 1, 2021
Commissioner Patrick asked –
 Understanding that there are several events that are going to
  be held at the So-Fi Stadium this month, will these new Antennas
  be up and running prior to the upcoming events?
   Mr. Fox stated if AT&T is approved this evening by the
  Planning Commission, they must still be able to be approved
  by the Building Division along with several other shops in
  City Hall, and so with that the site will not be constructed
  for some time before the antennas can go live.

Commissioner Rice asked –
 Who exactly will this new antenna system benefit or who will it
  be for? Cell phone users, for the public, attendees of So-Fi
  stadium only, the local community, first responders? Whom will
  benefit?
   Mr. Fox stated everyone you just mentioned – all of the above.
 You will be operating the antennas at 20mhz?
   Mr. Fox asked if his colleague and associate Mr. Bodewiser
  could come forward to answer the technical questions.
   Mr. Gary Bodewiser stated that with regards to how will the
  antennas operate at 20mhz?, well the frequencies are multi-
  use from 600mhz all the way up to 5ghz bandwidth. It will
  cover a different number of spectrums. Lower bandwidths will
  be for emergency services, public safety, which this site
  will be part of the national first network for first
  responders and this is primarily the focus of the site.
 Where is there a similar cell site like this one located near
  to this cell site, if there is one?
   Mr. Bodewiser stated there is another cell site in the area,
  but I don’t know exactly where they would be located. They
  are listed in the packet by staff.
 Just want to be clear, not asking about any of the local cell
  sites that are currently nearby, I am asking where if any, is
  there another facility with this type of antenna that is near
  here or any location in California?
   Mr. Bodewiser said, these are considered Macro-cell sites and
  AT&T has developed all of their Macro-cell sites in the same
  fashion, in order to work in similar fashion.

Commissioner Trejo asked both –
 Is this macro-cell site as large as it is because of the number
  of people who will be attending and the number of people
  anticipated to attend all of the entertainment venues, including
  both the IBEC and So-Fi arenas, including the nearby community?
   Mr. Bodewiser said it is one of the reasons, this site will
  be as large as it is, but it is important to cover this area
  to ensure that the first responders and important emergency
  personnel will be able to utilize their own bandwidth without
  any problems or interference in the middle of an emergency
  situation. We at AT&T decided it was important to make this
  happen.
 For first responders in this area, how is the system working
  for them?
   Mr. Bodewiser said in this area it does not. Without this
  cell-site they will not have access to their specific 600mghz
  signal. In working with other L.A. County Law Enforcement
  agencies, they are serviced in those areas and state the
  cameras that they have to wear will not work without having
  that particular internet signal.
 With the size of the new venues and the number of attendees
  along with the first responders, it is imperative that AT&T
  increase the service to make sure that not only any attendees
  2
 Inglewood Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
September 1, 2021
  but definitely the first responders will be able to ensure their
  success in performing their jobs.
   Mr. Bodewiser said it is for all to use, and in not singling
  out any one group over another, we know it is truly imperative
  that public safety for all does come first and that is truly
  AT&T’s number one concern.

Commissioner Shaw-Williams asked –
 With the ever changing and evolving internet and with technology
  increasing every day, will there come a time once this operation
  is up and running, that there will be a need for more of these
  antennas and will AT&T have to increase additional bandwidth or
  radio units?
   Mr. Bodewiser said that is a very hard question to answer. I
  don’t want to say yes that is true and I don’t want to say no
  it is not true, with the present plan for this antenna system,
  it is our design to last and work as most of the cell sites
  in the areas are now handled by computers, if say one site
  goes down or has a problem, the next cell site nearby will
  cover both areas until the repairs can be made. That is the
  way they are now set up. In the future, I can say that possibly
  the cell-site will need further assistance with all of the
  new technology that will be coming on board within the next
  six months to a year, Super Bowl, Olympics, etc.

Chairman Springs asked the planning commission for any final
questions or words.

Commissioner Rice asked Mr. Bodewiser –
 Regardless of the 600mhz and up to 5ghz, what is really important
  is the low-bandwidth that the first responders will be utilizing
  if needed, where it will prioritize the first responders over
  anyone else’s use, is that correct?
   Mr. Bodewiser stated Yes, that is correct and ultimately the
  way it is designed for everyone’s safety.
 So are you saying that in the long run the 600mhz and the
  computer internet linkage is really not needed, but possibly
  just extra nonessential bandwidth?
   Mr. Bodewiser said No, that is not correct, and not to sound
  harsh, but it is necessary for the full spectrum of the
  bandwidth, from the very high to the low bandwidth is utilized
  by the first responders. With the computer system and internet
  moving forward into 5ghz, it is very useful say there happened
  to be an event where first responders were utilizing their
  personal  internet  all  while  being  at  the  various
  entertainment events, and the call came out to the first
  responders to action, it would be important for those
  responders to have access to all of the bandwidth for
  recording, and tracking, and say the 600mhz hits capacity
  (which is called blocking), then the low bandwidth would still
  be accessible to the first responders in assisting them with
  doing their job effectively.
 You’re saying that this cell-site has override capabilities to
  ensure that there is enough bandwidth to cover this area.
   Mr. Bodewiser stated Yes, that is correct.

Commissioner Trejo asks Mr. Bodewiser –
 How long will it take for a system like this to get up and
  running?
   Mr. Bodewiser stated he would bring up Mr. Dan Fox to answer
  that question.
   Mr. Fox stated it would take about six months once all of the
  paperwork is complete, and they have AT&T’s permits.
